{"parentUuid":"3ce238e4-bbcc-4bdd-a3c3-29e461db6cb8","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"871c469d-8dd5-440e-9b1e-0b643bb2d2d3","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/yawoppong-krampah/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: since HEAD (uncommitted T06 work); ticket #7, spec #1"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"edb4d577-335b-4b1e-9a53-96b0d850fa1e","timestamp":"2026-10-12T04:45:19.553Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01StLmcC9R3wuYo3qPbZM575","session_id":"ed24a1e3-881f-4be6-a801-a77028a939ce","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/yawoppong-krampah/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"47994f02-dcad-41a7-8d5f-7405b25da6b2","version":"2.1.288","gitBranch":"main"}

The account counts are fetched only for Admin, and `test_an_editor_never_sees_account_numbers_anywhere` checks this.\n- **Vocabulary:** the Dashboard and Content list text matches `CONTEXT.md` (Published, Live, Deactivated accounts, Content list). \"Upcoming Events\" is not used.\n- **Escaping:** titles are autoescaped, and a test covers it.\n- **CSRF:** the new routes are GET-only.\n- **Dependencies:** none were added.\n\n**(b) Smells (all judgement calls)**\n\n`app/content.py`\n- **Primitive Obsession / hidden coupling:** `kind` and `status` are bare strings, and `f\"{kind}s\"` builds table names, dict keys (`f\"{status}_{kind}s\"`) and SQL. Pluralising by appending \"s\" ties the `posts` and `pages` table names to the dashboard key names. -&gt; A small mapping (type to table) or a tiny dataclass. This also removes the f-string SQL.\n- **Shotgun Surgery:** adding a type or status means editing `content.py`, the macro in `content_list.html`, four literal Dashboard links, `.row-*` CSS and the tests. -&gt; Drive the filter links and Dashboard stats from `TYPES`/`STATUSES` in a loop.\n\n`app/accounts.py`\n- **Data Clumps / Primitive Obsession:** `count_by_status` returns `(active, deactivated)`, and the template reads `account_counts[0]` and `[1]`. The order is easy to swap. -&gt; Return a dict or NamedTuple (`.active`, `.deactivated`). One `SELECT active, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY active` would also replace the two queries.\n\n`app/routes/admin.py`\n- **Mysterious Name:** the param `type` shadows the builtin. It is renamed `kind` and then `state` (for status) before reaching the template, so one concept has three names. -&gt; Use `type_`/`status` at the edge and `kind`/`status` after that. Do not use `state`, which collides with `app.state`.\n- **Duplicated Code (mild):** the account-count permission is checked in the route and again in the template (`account_counts and can(...)`). The comment justifies defence in depth, but `account_counts` being None already covers it. -&gt; Drop the template-side `can`.\n\n`templates/admin/dashboard.html`, `content_list.html`\n- **Duplicated Code:** the query string (`?type=..&amp;amp;status=..`) is hand-built four times on the Dashboard and again in the `link` macro. -&gt; One shared macro or helper, or `route()` with query params.\n- `account_counts[0]` / `[1]` in the template (see Data Clumps above).\n\n`templates/base.html`\n- **Divergent Change:** about 25 lines of page-specific CSS (`.stats`, `.filters`, `.row-*`) are inlined into the shared layout. This replaces the `&lt;link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"{{ css_path | default('style.css') }}\"&gt;` hook. Every later UI ticket will edit `base.html`. -&gt; Move the CSS to a stylesheet. Check that nothing still passes `css_path` to the admin base (`templates/public/base.html` is separate).\n\n`app/web.py`\n- `stamp` is a vague name. -&gt; `format_utc_minute`, or similar.\n- It also hard-codes \"UTC\" and a string slice, so it breaks silently if the stored format changes.\n\n`tests/test_t06_dashboard.py`\n- **Duplicated Code:** the two \"through its life\" tests are near-identical. -&gt; Parametrize over post and page.\n- `from tests.test_t02_posts import ...` is repeated inside two functions, and the tests import helpers from other ticket test files (`test_t03_publish`, `test_t05_pages`). -&gt; Move the shared helpers to `conftest.py`.\n- `FOUR` is a mysterious name, and `counts()` uses hyphenated keys while `content.counts` uses underscores.\n\n`CONTEXT.md` vocabulary (minor)\n- The SQL alias and template variable `author_name` hold a Display name, and `row-author` is the CSS class. -&gt; Name them `display_name` to match the glossary.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>57459</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>6</tool_uses><duration_ms>33997</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Verdict:** every acceptance criterion in #7 is implemented. I found no missing requirements and no clearly wrong implementation. I only read the diff and ran no tests, so nothing below was run. The main weaknesses are two thin tests.\n\n**Criteria, one by one**\n- **Four counts for every user.** Met. `content.counts` is read fresh per request and zero-filled. Spec #1 story 46: \"show the four content counts but no account counts.\"\n- **Account counts Admin-only.** Met. The route fetches them only if `allowed(role, \"dashboard.account_counts\")`, the template re-checks `can(...)`, and the permission rule is in `RULES`. Ticket: \"numbers are not reachable by a direct request.\"\n  - No endpoint exposes account counts, so there is nothing to request directly.\n  - `test_account_numbers_cannot_be_asked_for_by_a_direct_request` probes mostly nonexistent URLs. Those return 404, so it proves little. The real protection is covered by `test_an_editor_never_sees_account_numbers_anywhere`.\n- **Reminder text.** Met. `#live-reminder` names `cms publish` and `cms deploy`. Tests assert \"changes not live yet\" is absent.\n- **Filters separately and together.** Met. All 8 combinations are parametrized. Unknown values are ignored, which is harmless and tested.\n- **Row fields.** Met. Title, status, Display name via the `users.display_name` join, and updated time are shown. The username never appears, and there is a test for that.\n- **~390 px.** Met in implementation: stacked rows, a flex-wrap filter bar, and `auto-fit` tiles. Screenshots at 390 px are committed.\n  - `test_the_screens_are_built_for_a_phone_width` is close to vacuous. It passes if the page contains `\"flex-wrap\"` anywhere.\n- **Immediate update.** Met. There is no caching, and lifecycle tests cover create, publish, unpublish and delete for both Posts and Pages.\n- **Tests at the admin HTTP seam.** Met. They use `client_as` and cover each role, the reminder, every filter combination and the row fields.\n\n**(b) Unrequested behaviour (all minor)**\n- The count tiles link to pre-filtered lists, and there are \"All content\" and \"Dashboard\" links. These are reasonable navigation, but the ticket didn't ask for them.\n- Rows show a Post/Page type label. The ticket's row list omits it, but a mixed list needs it.\n- Sorting is by most recently updated, which the ticket doesn't specify. Account tiles also link to the user list.\n- The dashboard shows \"Signed in as …\", and a Page with no Author renders \"—\".\n- Several tests pin incidental details: exactly one `&lt;form&gt;` on the Dashboard, a CSRF-token check, and `&lt;table` being absent.\n- The `stamp` filter formats times as \"… UTC\" truncated to the minute. That is fine, and the full ISO value is kept in `datetime`.\n\n**(c) Possibly wrong**\n- None. Each row's name is the Author's current Display name, which matches the spec's byline rule.\n\n**Edits to existing files**\n- **`tests/test_t00.py` and `tests/test_t01_auth.py`: justified.** The tests asserted the placeholder \"hello admin\", and T06 replaces that text. The new `&lt;h1&gt;Dashboard&lt;/h1&gt;` assertions keep the same intent, including the negative check that signed-out visitors don't see dashboard content.\n- **`templates/base.html`, inline CSS: justified, with a caveat.**\n  - The old `&lt;link href=\"style.css\"&gt;` was dead in the admin: no static mount exists, and the relative path resolved to a 404 under `/admin/...`. `css_path` is unused anywhere.\n  - Inline CSS is needed to meet the phone-width criterion, and it avoids an absolute path.\n  - The caveat is that it bloats `base.html`, which every admin screen shares. A single new `&lt;style&gt;` block would block a future strict CSP, but none exists today.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>57009</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>12</tool_uses><duration_ms>39925</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

{"parentUuid":"0f6c7a57-957a-497e-8b65-67bc9b469af5","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CfwjgDGjoDY7qig7zALKR","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T06 (#7) is implemented and committed to `main` as `db7d6de`, whose message ends `Closes #7`. The issue is still open: I didn't push, and a closing keyword only takes effect once it reaches GitHub.\n\n- **Dashboard:** Every signed-in user sees the four content counts (Published Posts, Draft Posts, Published Pages, Draft Pages). Only the Admin also sees active and Deactivated account counts. The server fetches those only for the Admin, so an Editor's pages never contain them. The reminder that marking content Published doesn't make it Live until `cms publish` and `cms deploy` run is there, with no \"Changes not live yet\" indicator.\n- **Content list:** The new `/admin/content` page lists Posts and Pages together. You can filter by type, by status, or both. Each row shows title, type, status, Display name and last-updated time. The newest-updated item comes first. A filter value the page doesn't recognise is ignored.\n- **Added beyond the ticket:** The Dashboard count tiles link to the matching filtered list. A Page with no Author shows \"—\" for its Display name.\n- **Existing tests changed:** Two older tests (`test_t00` and `test_t01_auth`) asserted the old placeholder text \"hello admin\". They now assert the Dashboard heading.\n- **Phone width:** The admin had no working stylesheet (the old `style.css` link 404s under `/admin`), so I put a small inline one in `templates/base.html`. I rendered both screens at 390 px in headless Chrome and checked there was no horizontal scroll. The screenshots are in `docs/screenshots/T06-*-390px.png`. The automated phone-width test only checks the viewport meta tag and that no `<table>` is used, so the screenshots are the real evidence.\n- **Review:**\n  - **Standards:** `/code-review` found no hard violations. I fixed two smells: positional `account_counts[0]`/`[1]` and the `type` parameter shadowing the builtin.\n  - **Spec:** Every acceptance criterion is implemented. I left the other smells unchanged, with reasons.\n  - **Issue comment:** The findings and how I resolved each are posted on issue #7.\n- **Not committed:** `notes/usage-ledger.csv` and the session transcripts. They go in the separate docs commits you've been using. `.claude/state/phase` is set to `T06`.
